repository.name: @webex/common-timers
repository.purpose: Timer primitives for the Cisco Webex JS SDK that never hold a Node process open: unref-ing wrappers over setTimeout and setInterval, plus a restartable one-shot Timer with a guarded init-running-done lifecycle.

public_interfaces.name: package exports
public_interfaces.audience: Ten workspace packages inside the Webex JS SDK plus external npm consumers of @webex/common-timers.
public_interfaces.notes: Verify names and types against src/index.ts, and the compatibility commitments against the Public surface and Export stability sections of src/docs/README.md. The exported handle type is the union number or NodeJS.Timeout.

public_interfaces.notes: The declared aggregate test script chains test:integration and test:browser, neither of which this package defines, so it cannot succeed. Use test:unit and test:style individually.

glossary.definition: Asking a Node timer handle to stop counting toward process liveness, so a pending timer cannot prevent the process from exiting.
glossary.notes: Available only on Node timer handles. Browsers return a number with no such method, which is why every wrapper feature-detects it.

glossary.definition: In safeSetTimeout and safeSetInterval, specifically safe against wedging a process open.
glossary.notes: It implies nothing about error handling, argument validation, or type safety.

glossary.definition: The value the host scheduler returns: a Timeout object in Node, a number in a browser. The package returns it unchanged after unref-ing it.
glossary.notes: Callers pass it to the platform clearTimeout or clearInterval; the package exports no clear function.

glossary.definition: Move a Timer from init to running by scheduling its callback.
glossary.notes: Only start arms a timer. Construction schedules nothing.

glossary.definition: Clear a running Timer and re-arm it for the full original timeout.
glossary.notes: It is an idle deadline, not a pause or a resume; the remaining time is discarded.

glossary.definition: The terminal Timer state, reached by either expiry or cancellation.
glossary.notes: It is not recoverable, and the two causes are indistinguishable to a caller.

evidence_rules.requirement: Emit a command only when its script exists in package.json and the workspace-scoped invocation was verified to run.
evidence_rules.notes: The declared aggregate test script is the counterexample: it is present in package.json but cannot succeed, so it is never emitted as a runnable command.

evidence_rules.requirement: Emit an export name only when it is declared in src/index.ts and reachable through the entry point declared by main or devMain.
Ground every behavior claim in the implementation, and state separately whether a test observes it. Nine Timer lifecycle branches are tested; the unref behavior is not.
evidence_rules.notes: Commit history is not acceptable rationale evidence for this package.

evidence_rules.requirement: Never ship a template placeholder in a generated document; replace it with verified repository evidence or surface the gap as a blocking question.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not infer the runtime platform; feature-detect unref on the returned handle.
negative_guidance.why: One module and one build serve both Node and the browser. A platform branch would add a conditional export or bundler shim the package has deliberately avoided.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not turn an invalid Timer transition into a silent no-op.
negative_guidance.why: Consumers rely on the throw being loud, and the message wording is asserted by regular expression in the unit suite.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not treat reset as a pause or resume.
negative_guidance.why: It restores the full original timeout by design; both production consumers use it as an idle deadline.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not add a runtime dependency without escalating.
negative_guidance.why: The package currently declares none, which is what removes every cycle and third-party failure mode from the eleven workspace packages that consume it.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not cite commit or pull-request history as rationale for current behavior.
negative_guidance.why: The package owner verified during onboarding that its history is dominated by release chores and repo-wide sweeps, so it cannot explain why behavior exists.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not publish a Repo Standards template out of .sdd/templates into docs.
negative_guidance.why: Authoring templates stay hidden; only instantiated, repository-grounded documents belong in the visible documentation tree.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not treat a green unit run as proof that the unref contract still holds.
negative_guidance.why: No test asserts that unref() is called, so removing it from src/index.ts leaves the suite green. The module's core guarantee is currently supported by code reading only; see the Verification section of src/docs/README.md.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not trust a green unit run after changing src without rebuilding first.
negative_guidance.why: The suite imports the package by name, which resolves through main to dist/, so it validates the built artifact rather than the source.

high.expectation: The claim is backed by src/index.ts or test/unit/spec/index.ts and the affected specification sections are updated in the same change.

medium.expectation: Implementation evidence exists but no test observes the behavior, as with the unref calls. Record the gap in the Verification section rather than asserting verified coverage.

low.expectation: Neither code nor tests establish the fact. Stop and ask the package owner; do not fall back to commit history or to a plausible default.

fallback_rules: When code and this context disagree, the code wins; correct the context and the affected specification sections in the same change.
When a fact cannot be established from src/index.ts, test/unit/spec/index.ts, or package.json, stop and ask the package owner rather than inferring it from commit history.
